feature: IN-list membership predicates in WHERE clauses

scenarios.name: IN matches rows whose data-lane value is a listed member
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — expressions/list (IN membership on a value)
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.kind IN ["neighbor"] RETURN n.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id

scenarios.name: IN with several numeric members matches any of them
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — expressions/list (IN over multiple numeric members)
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.severity_score IN [10, 30] RETURN n.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id

scenarios.name: IN with a single-element list matches just that value
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.kind IN ["island"] RETURN n.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id

scenarios.name: IN with an empty list matches nothing
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.kind IN [] RETURN n.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id

scenarios.name: IN list containing null — null is not a member, other values still match
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.severity_score IN [null, 20] RETURN n.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id

scenarios.name: IN on a spine field with element-level params
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — expressions/list (IN with parameterized members)
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.entity_id IN [$first, $second] RETURN n.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id

scenarios.name: IN narrows the aggregation path before the COUNT
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — expressions/list (IN filter applied before aggregation)
scenarios.query: MATCH (h)-[:PG_LINKS__grid_fixtures]->(n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.kind IN ["neighbor"] RETURN h.entity_id AS src, COUNT(n) AS c

scenarios.name: IN composes with AND
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — expressions/list (IN composed with AND)
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.kind IN ["island"] AND n.data.severity_score > 10 RETURN n.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id

scenarios.name: NOT over IN with a null list member keeps non-members (two-valued logic)
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — expressions/list (NOT over IN with a null member; two-valued divergence from Cypher's three-valued IN)
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE NOT (n.data.severity_score IN [10, null, 30]) RETURN n.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id

scenarios.name: non-list IN right-hand side is rejected
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — expressions/list (non-list IN right-hand side is rejected)
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.severity_score IN 5 RETURN n.entity_id AS id

scenarios.name: IN with a null left-hand side (unset tag) is a non-member, not an error
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — expressions/list (null/unobserved left-hand side is a non-member under two-valued logic, never an error)
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.tags.zone IN ["core", "edge"] RETURN n.entity_id AS id ORDER BY id

scenarios.name: a string member against a numeric field is rejected — no cross-type coercion (type-strictness)
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — expressions/list (Cypher returns false for 10 IN ["10"]; TAP is a typed graph and the declared schema is the type oracle, so a string member against an integer-declared field is rejected outright rather than coerced (the ORM would cast to Int4) or silently dropped — req-grid-traversal-lang-type-strictness)
scenarios.query: MATCH (n:grid_fixtures__node) WHERE n.data.severity_score IN ["10", "20"] RETURN n.entity_id AS id
